answer.summary: Ray says TikTok uses annual planning as a baseline, then iterates during the year and quarterly so it can pivot nimbly with market conditions. Long-term strategy stays steady, while how to realize it is continuously experimented with; this faster cycle also shortens product feedback and go-to-market loops.

sections.heading: Planning cadence and flexibility
sections.content: TikTok has an annual planning cycle, but Ray describes it as a baseline rather than a fixed plan: the company makes many iterations midyear and quarterly, allowing it to pivot nimbly toward what it sees in the market.

sections.heading: What changes—and what stays constant
sections.content: Some long-term strategy remains stable: Ray gives the example of creating inspiring, frictionless, immersive user experiences. By contrast, how to realize that strategy is subject to consistent experimentation. He says this about his experience in advertising products and notes he cannot speak for the user-product side. Because the roadmap is less static, product feedback and go-to-market loops become shorter and faster.
